english: A fair die is rolled, and if it shows the number $k$, an urn is filled with $k$ white balls and $6-k$ black balls. Three balls are then drawn from the urn one after another without replacement. Given that the first two balls drawn are white, the conditional probability that the third ball drawn is also white is ______.
hindi: एक अनभिनत पासा फेंका जाता है, तथा यदि उस पर संख्या $k$ आती है, तो एक कलश में $k$ सफेद गेंदें तथा $6-k$ काली गेंदें भरी जाती हैं। फिर कलश से तीन गेंदें एक के बाद एक बिना प्रतिस्थापन के निकाली जाती हैं। दिया है कि पहली दो निकाली गई गेंदें सफेद हैं, तो तीसरी निकाली गई गेंद के भी सफेद होने की सप्रतिबन्ध प्रायिकता ______ है।
solution: Required $=\dfrac{210/720}{70/180}=\dfrac{3}{4}=0.75$; equivalently the Bayes posterior of $k$ is $\propto k(k-1)$ and $\sum\dfrac{k(k-1)}{70}\cdot\dfrac{k-2}{4}=\dfrac{210}{280}$
solution_full: Let $K$ be the number on the die and $W_{i}$ the event that the $i$-th ball is white. Given $K=k$, by the multiplication theorem for draws without replacement: $P(W_{1}\cap W_{2}\mid K=k)=\dfrac{k}{6}\cdot\dfrac{k-1}{5}=\dfrac{k(k-1)}{30}$ and $P(W_{1}\cap W_{2}\cap W_{3}\mid K=k)=\dfrac{k(k-1)(k-2)}{120}$.

Law of total probability over $k=1,\dots,6$: $P(W_{1}\cap W_{2})=\dfrac{1}{6}\cdot\dfrac{0+2+6+12+20+30}{30}=\dfrac{70}{180}=\dfrac{7}{18}$ and $P(W_{1}\cap W_{2}\cap W_{3})=\dfrac{1}{6}\cdot\dfrac{0+0+6+24+60+120}{120}=\dfrac{210}{720}=\dfrac{7}{24}$.
Conditional probability: $P(W_{3}\mid W_{1}\cap W_{2})=\dfrac{P(W_{1}\cap W_{2}\cap W_{3})}{P(W_{1}\cap W_{2})}=\dfrac{7/24}{7/18}=\dfrac{18}{24}=\dfrac{3}{4}$.

The same through Bayes' theorem: $P(K=k\mid W_{1}\cap W_{2})=\dfrac{k(k-1)}{70}$ (so the urn with $6$ white balls has posterior $\dfrac{30}{70}$); then $P(W_{3}\mid W_{1}\cap W_{2})=\sum_{k}\dfrac{k(k-1)}{70}\cdot\dfrac{k-2}{4}=\dfrac{210}{280}=0.75$.
originality_note: New: an urn whose composition is set by a die roll, observed through two white draws without replacement, and asked for the next draw; the posterior on the composition is proportional to k(k - 1) (way 5: multiplication theorem, total probability and Bayes linked in one prediction). Closest known: the two-ball urn puzzle on cut-the-knot and Laplace's rule of succession. Different because: the prior comes from a die, draws are without replacement, and the answer is a ratio of two total-probability sums.
blueprint_concepts: Conditional probability and the reduced sample space

concept_use.Conditional probability and the reduced: The answer is P(W3 | W1 n W2) = P(W1 W2 W3)/P(W1 W2), a conditional probability.
concept_use.Multiplication theorem: P(W1 n W2 | K = k) and P(W1 n W2 n W3 | K = k) are products of successive draw probabilities (multiplication theorem).
concept_use.Law of total probability: P(W1 n W2) and P(W1 n W2 n W3) are sums over the six values of k (law of total probability).
concept_use.Bayes' theorem: The posterior P(K = k | W1 n W2) = k(k - 1)/70 is Bayes' theorem, used in the second route.
